attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own newsletter, stated as his view.

semantics.note: Two parts: a present-tense denial of 5GW now, plus a firm 'nor will there be' forecast of 10GW more in 2027. Keeping the first part in the present matches his wording. The surrounding end-2026 framing is flagged in the contract.

contract.note: Treating capacity as powered, procurable capacity and counting the 2027 increment without double-counting is an ordinary reading. Requiring operational records over announcements fits his point about how fast compute comes online.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure of an up-to-5GW Amazon deal, with nearly 1GW from Amazon by end-2026. It covers one provider only, is not a full inventory, and says nothing about what comes online in 2027.

reviews.rationale: The 2027 forecast is not due until the year ends. For the present-tense part, the packet has only one company disclosure about a single provider. That cannot show whether total capacity Anthropic could buy was above or below 5GW at publication. Neither part is settled.

attribution.note: His own sentence. The nearby reference to his earlier piece does not change who is making the claim.

semantics.note: Firm 'won't exist' attached to the antecedent 'once the AI bubble bursts'. The antecedent is kept and no deadline is added.

contract.note: Reading the claim as broad disappearance of the venture-backed customer group, rather than a single failure, is fair. The contract labels the claim 'retrospective', which is a minor mislabel; it does not affect the result.

evidence.note: IMF, 13 Oct 2026: markets resilient, with an AI correction named only as a risk. It does not show the antecedent (a burst) has happened.

reviews.rationale: Conditional forecast with no deadline. By the cutoff the only evidence (IMF) treats an AI correction as a possible future shock, so the bubble-burst antecedent is unknown or has not occurred. Under the policy the consequent cannot be scored.

attribution.note: His own assertion in his own article.

semantics.note: The causal core is kept: speculative capital acting on overestimated compute demand drives chip demand. The 'magnitudes larger' belief is compressed but not distorted.

contract.note: Taking the claim as a major driver across the market, and 'everybody' as a broad description rather than literal, is an ordinary reading. Requiring evidence of both overestimation and its causal role is appropriate.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's own blog about funding infrastructure for labs. It shows forward-looking investment, not whether demand is overestimated.
Microsoft's own statement that demand exceeds capacity. It cuts against his claim but is a company talking about itself, not a representative causal test.

reviews.rationale: The packet has only two company disclosures, pointing in opposite directions. There is no representative data tying purchasers' demand expectations to chip orders and actual paid use, so the causal claim can be neither supported nor contradicted.

attribution.note: His own sentence. The phrase 'branded as insatiable demand' describes others' framing, which he then rejects in his own voice.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'almost entirely' and 'mostly' qualifiers, the step that the potential comes from OpenAI and Anthropic, and his description of the labs.

contract.note: Using NVIDIA's latest reported quarter before the post is a reasonable choice of window, and it is flagged. 'Mostly' read as more than half and 'almost entirely' as nearly all are ordinary readings.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's 10-Q shows revenue concentrated in a few customers, including one AI lab with a meaningful share. It does not split growth into speculative and non-speculative shares.
Anthropic's S-1 shows net losses through H1 2026, mostly from fair-value changes. That bears on 'unprofitable' for one lab only. A stated risk factor does not show the spending is unsustainable.

reviews.rationale: No evidence divides NVIDIA's revenue growth between speculative purchases and established workloads, or measures the two labs' share of the expected spending. The Anthropic filing only partly supports the 'unprofitable' description, and for one lab. The core causal claim is not settled.
